1 لَعَجَ , aor.
لَعَجَ , (inf. n. لَعْجٌ, TA) It (a beating, TA) burned the skin: it pained the body: (K:) it (a beating) pained a person, and burned the skin: (S:) it (anything burning) pained: it (love, or grief,) burned his heart. (TA.) [See بَعَجَ.] لَاعِجٌ is numbered amongst the [few] inf. ns. of the measure فَاعِلٌ [like قَائِمٌ]; and means as explained below. (TA.) ―
-b2- لَعَجَ فى الصَّدْرِ It (an affair) was unsettle in the bosom; syn. خَلَخَ. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
